title: POC Access Tiering and PII Scrub Playbook
body:
Overview:

Quick working guide for POCs where the customer requires: tiered access controls, on-ingress PII scrubbing/pseudonymization, short telemetry retention, and a DPA addendum template that references customer-controlled KMS and redaction guarantees. This is intended for SEs running field pilots or pilot-to-prod pilots where legal asks are lightweight but must be tracked and demonstrably implemented.

Goals (POC scope):
- Provide reference architecture for: 1) role-based access + least-privilege on telemetry and persisted artifacts; 2) deterministic PII scrubbing on ingress with configurable policies; 3) retention windows for different data classes; 4) audit trails to support DPA addendum requests.
- Deliver a small set of implementation patterns we can show to customers in 1-2 weeks.

Non-goals:
- This is not an exhaustive compliance certification. Not intended to replace customer legal review or a full SOC2/ISO deliverable.

Key definitions (keep simple for customers):
- Ingress copy: raw request payload captured at the API front door (short-lived, never persisted unless explicitly enabled).
- Persisted artifact: any object we write to object storage, DB, or long-term logs (conversations, eval records).
- Telemetry: metrics/traces and low-cardinality logs used for debugging.
- PII (operational): email, phone, SSN/Tax IDs, account numbers, full name when linked to account id, and customer-specified sensitive tokens.

Recommended patterns (practical):
1) Access tiering (3-tier model)
   - Tier A: Customer-managed artifacts (customer KMS-protected, only accessible via customer-provided credentials or Redwoods' customer-service role). Short path: used for customer-owned conversation logs when customer elects Private or Dedicated.
   - Tier B: POC artifacts (SE debug artifacts, short retention, encrypted with Redwood-managed KMS, access limited to SE + 1 product PM).
   - Tier C: Aggregate telemetry (prometheus/grafana metrics, sampled traces). No PII. Retention default 30 days for POC unless customer asks otherwise.
   - Implementation notes: map these to roles in IAM (e.g., redwood:se, redwood:engineer, customer:admin) and enforce at resource label level. Use per-bucket IAM bindings for S3/GCS.

2) Ingress PII scrubber (pluggable pipeline)
   - Two modes: quick-scrub (regex + blocklist) for low-friction POCs; deep-scrub (ML-based named entity recognition + contextual heuristics) for sensitive pilots.
   - Quick-scrub heuristics: email regex, phone number patterns (international), credit card PAN detection using Luhn, short token blacklist. Configurable allowlist for false-positives via tenant config.
   - Deep-scrub: run NER model (open-source) then pseudonymize names and ID-like entities; maintain mapping only if customer opts-in (mapping stored in Tier A under customer control).

3) Pseudonymization vs Redaction tradeoffs
   - Redaction: replace sensitive spans with [REDACTED]. Lowest risk, breaks context for debugging.
   - Pseudonymization: replace with stable token (user_1234). Allows debugging and session stitching. Store mapping under Tier A or ephemeral cache (TTL 24h) depending on consent.

4) Retention windows (suggested defaults for POC)
   - Raw ingress copy: 0–24 hours, default 0 (not persisted).
   - Pseudonymized conversation transcripts (Tier B): 7 days.
   - Aggregated/hashed metrics: 90 days.
   - Audit logs (who accessed what): 365 days (may be reduced to 90 per customer contract).

DPA addendum snippets (draft language)
- Minimal retention clause (example): "Provider will not persist raw request payloads beyond 24 hours unless Customer explicitly enables persistence. Where persistence is enabled, Provider will apply Customer-selected PII minimization rules prior to storage."
- Key control clause (example): "Customer may elect to supply and control the encryption key(s) used to protect persisted customer artifacts; Provider will not have access to plaintext without customer-supplied credentials."
- Redaction guarantee (example): "Provider will implement configured redaction/pseudonymization at ingress and will provide automated verification artifacts on request (sampled diffs showing removed spans)."

Operational checklist for SE (what we demo in pilot):
- Confirm customer wants quick-scrub vs deep-scrub. Ticket: JIRA-PS-4123.
- Create dedicated S3/GCS bucket for POC Tier B, bind to IAM role redwood:se-access.
- Enable ingress scrubber on the API gateway (config: scrub_mode=quick, allowlist=[company.com]).
- Spin up ephemeral pseudonymization cache (Redis) with TTL 24h; note mapping persists only if customer signs opt-in.
- Hook audit logging to separate secure bucket and ensure retention policy set to 365d.

Security/ops considerations:
- Sampling: never export raw customer requests to external analytics without explicit consent. Use hashed fingerprints for debugging.
- Rollback plan: if scrubber causes high false-positive rate, a 'release hold' flag flips to pseudonymize-only mode and route full requests to Tier A for customer review.
- Data access review: monthly access review for Tier B artifacts; automated daily email to SE + customer admin listing any access events.

Testing and validation (must-have for legal sign-off):
- Unit tests for regex scrub rules with positive/negative samples.
- End-to-end test: simulate 100 sample requests containing seeded PII, verify scrubber removes/replaces per policy. Store test report in Confluence link above.
- Sampling audit: example script that pulls 50 random persisted transcripts and runs a high-recall PII detector to estimate residual PII recall/precision.

Open questions / decisions (for next SE sync):
- Customer default: do we set persisted transcripts to pseudonymize or redact? (Action: confirm with CSM prior to field test).
- KMS arrangement: support bring-your-own-key in POC timeline? (Answer impacts infra work; templated Jenkinsfile and infra PR linked).
- Telemetry retention for EU customers: do we need separate retention window for EU? (Likely yes — map to customer region.)

Action items (owners):
- Maya: produce quick-start SE playbook with terraform module for Tier B bucket and IAM (due 2025-02-28).
- Ethan: prototype quick-scrub pipeline using lua/nginx filter + regex set (due 2025-02-21).
- Priya: draft DPA addendum language and circulate to legal (due 2025-03-03).
- Liam: add e2e scrub test harness and sample report in Confluence (due 2025-02-24).

Notes for demos and customer conversations:
- Keep language simple: "We remove or obfuscate sensitive fields before they hit long-term storage."
- Offer two knobs: retention window and pseudonymization vs redaction.
- For enterprise pilots, push for customer KMS even if not strictly required — simplifies legal.

Appendix: quick regex examples (not production ready)
- Email: /[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/
- US phone: /(?:\+1[-.\s]?)?\(?\d{3}\)?[-.\s]?\d{3}[-.\s]?\d{4}/
- Credit card PAN (Luhn precheck): /(?:4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})?|5[1-5][0-9]{14})/
